title: Ignore vanished entries during Vaporize source-gate discovery
description: Vaporize aborted a Windows Savepoint installation before build when live directory enumeration encountered an entry that had vanished or could no longer be resolved, surfacing NSCocoaErrorDomain Code 4 instead of continuing discovery.

historicalContent.expectedBehavior: Source-gate discovery skips transiently unavailable entries while preserving ordinary file and directory traversal semantics.
currentEvidence: The original Savepoint install failed during mandatory i18n source-gate discovery with NSCocoaErrorDomain Code 4 and WindowsError Code 3.
Vaporize now treats an unavailable resource-value observation as a vanished entry and skips only that entry's descendants.
All six sourceGate tests pass on Windows, including the vanished-entry regression fixture.
A real debug Savepoint CLI installation completed and the installed executable hash matched the built artifact.
acceptanceCriteria: A vanished discovery candidate does not abort the source gate.
Ordinary files remain distinguishable from unavailable entries.
Existing source-gate traversal tests remain green.
Vaporize installs the Savepoint CLI successfully on Windows.
historicalContent.scopeBoundary: This fix changes only source-gate filesystem observation; it does not weaken i18n findings or alter build and installation policy.
